Monkestation Chem Recipe Book

Recipes the chemistry simulator has worked out from the game code. Sections are collapsed to start with: open one, pick a gear tier, open a type, open a recipe and follow the numbered steps.

Section 1 · Medborg chem nade recipes

Medical cyborg chem nades

Foam and smoke grenades mixed with the medborg's own syringe and beaker from a chem dispenser. Pick your gear tier inside.

▸ Click to open the medborg recipes▾ Click to close
How to make a borg chem nade the idea, what you need, how to read a recipe

The idea

You carry a syringe and a beaker. You make a small trigger chemical and move it into the syringe, then build the payload chemical in the beaker, then inject the whole syringe into the beaker in one go. The trigger reacts with what is in the beaker and the contents burst out as foam or smoke, carrying the payload over many tiles.

  • Foam trigger = fluorosurfactant (made from fluorine, carbon and sulfuric acid), reacting with water in the beaker. Foam is slippery on its own, copies the payload about 3.2 times into each tile and lasts 8 seconds. Tiles = 2 x the units of trigger.
  • Smoke trigger = phosphorus, reacting with potassium and sugar in the beaker. Smoke lasts 20 seconds, covers 3 tiles per unit of trigger and puts the full payload in every tile, which people breathe in. It is not slippery.
  • Some recipes (metal foam, vortexes, spawns) have no syringe step: the last dispenser click is the trigger.

What you need

  • A Medical (or Science) cyborg with the syringe and the beaker storage apparatus, and a chem dispenser (the recipes assume the basic reagent list).
  • The apparatus starts with a 100u large beaker, and the medical beaker upgrade (second apparatus) also comes with a 100u beaker, but either can be swapped for any other beaker, such as a 300u bluespace beaker. These pages assume that if a borg can use a beaker size at all, it has two beakers of that size. No mixed sizes. (Using the second beaker as a staging area is not modelled yet.)
  • Syringe sizes: 15u stock, 60u with the bluespace syringe upgrade.
  • A chem heater for any recipe whose needs say so (unverified that a borg can use one).

How to read a recipe

  • Do the steps in order. The grey line under each step is what the beaker and syringe should hold afterwards: use it to catch a wrong click.
  • Tracking your place: every step starts green. Click a step when you have done it and it turns red and greyed with a FINISHED stamp (click again to undo). The orange Reset all steps button at the top of each recipe clears them. Progress is not saved: reopening or refreshing the page resets everything.
  • Bold boxed text is what matters in a step: the units (blue), the chemical (purple) and any SPILL / EMPTY command (red). The small grey bracket after a chemical says which dispenser button to press and how many times.
  • When several neighbouring dispenser steps add the same number of units, they are shown as one step with a numbered list: do them top to bottom, in that order. The tool picks click sizes so that you change dispenser buttons as rarely as possible, so 20u may be shown as two 10u clicks because the next chemical is also 10u. The beaker still ends up exactly the same.
  • "Dispenser: 45u water (a 30u click, then a 15u click)" means exactly those buttons. The dispenser offers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 50 and 100 unit buttons, and a click never puts in more than the free space in the beaker.
  • Tiles is how far the foam or smoke spreads. Per tick is how much payload lands on each tile every 0.2 s (foam) or 2 s (smoke) tick. Beaker used is how full the beaker was when it fired: recipes are tuned to use all of it.
  • "Order matters" means a wrong order makes a different reaction. "Any order works" means the dispense order does not change the result.

Click flow (from the code, not tested in a round)

  • Load the beaker into the dispenser with the apparatus. Clicks pass through to the beaker it holds. Right-click the machine with it to take the beaker back out.
  • Syringe: use it in hand to cycle the transfer amount; right-click a container to draw, left-click to inject.
  • Right-click with the apparatus to spill the beaker.

Stand clear afterwards: foam knocks people down. If any click detail differs on your server, please open an issue on GitHub; that is the most useful report.

Section 2 · Chemistry recipes, no upgrades

Chemistry recipes

Medicines and useful chemicals anyone can make from a chem dispenser alone: no other department, no special ingredients. Pick your beaker size inside.

▸ Click to open the chemistry recipes▾ Click to close
How to read a chemistry recipe clicks, heating, leftovers
  • Click each step when done: green = to do, red with FINISHED = done. The orange Reset all steps button at the top of a recipe clears it; nothing is saved when you close the page.
  • Do the steps in order, in one beaker. The grey line under each step is what the beaker should hold afterwards: use it to catch a wrong click.
  • Bold boxed text is what matters in a step: the units (blue), the chemical (purple) and any SPILL / EMPTY command (red). The grey bracket after a chemical says which dispenser button to press and how many times.
  • When several neighbouring dispenser steps add the same number of units, they are shown as one step with a numbered list: do them top to bottom, in that order. The tool picks click sizes so that you change dispenser buttons as rarely as possible, so 20u may be shown as two 10u clicks because the next chemical is also 10u. The beaker still ends up exactly the same.
  • "Dispenser: 25u water (a 25u click)" means that button. The dispenser offers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 50 and 100 unit buttons and a click never adds more than the free space in the beaker, so a recipe can end on a click that fills the beaker exactly.
  • "Heat to 390 K" means a chem heater. It only approaches the target temperature, so recipes aim 20 K above what the reaction needs. Wait until the beaker is at that temperature.
  • Every reaction here is instant (pH and purity are switched off on this server). A recipe sometimes makes by-products or leaves a few units of an ingredient: the Result line says what, and none of it matters for the product.
  • Dosing lines come from the reagent code: the overdose threshold and how long 1u lasts in the blood.
  • Nothing here has been tested in a live round.
Planned: other borg types. Service and any other cyborg with the tools. Similar recipes with small differences (usually one beaker, possibly no syringe upgrade). Which borgs can do this still has to be checked in the code.
